comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized Dutch title Scheikundige Technologie and the English title Chemical Engineering and Chemistry identify the same current TU/e academic programme. Current official programme and study-guide material accounts for all 180 EC as a 120-EC Chemical Engineering and Chemistry major and Bachelor College core, including the Bachelor Final Project, a 15-EC Impact of Technology learning line and 45 EC of elective space. Current 2026-2027 course records substantiate the compulsory formation in chemistry, materials and process engineering and the concluding project. The announced language-track change from 2027-2028 does not change the present target's academic curriculum and is not used to alter its normalized identity.
components: Chemical Engineering and Chemistry major and Bachelor College core programme, including Bachelor Final Project

Compulsory formation in calculus, chemistry, chemical bonding and spectroscopy, inorganic and organic chemistry, thermodynamics, kinetics and electrochemistry, materials, transport phenomena, chemical reactors, separation and process technology, laboratory and characterisation work, computational and data methods, challenge-based molecules-and-materials and process-design projects, and the Bachelor Final Project.
Required Impact of Technology formation within the official bachelor structure.
Genuine elective space preserved from the official curriculum structure.

exception.reason: Chemical Engineering and Chemistry at TU/e is a cumulative laboratory and process-engineering degree. Its compulsory formation progresses through calculus, practical inorganic, organic and physical chemistry, chemical bonding and spectroscopy, thermodynamics, reaction kinetics and electrochemistry, materials and their characterisation, transport phenomena, separation technology, chemical reactors, process technology and control, and repeated molecules-and-materials and process-design projects before a discipline-specific Bachelor Final Project. UCR offers biochemistry, molecular and cellular biology, one life-science laboratory, environmental chemistry within a circular-economy course, sustainability, mathematics, numerical methods, data science and renewable-system design. It does not offer the required general, inorganic, organic, analytical and physical chemistry sequence; thermodynamics and transport phenomena; reactor, separation and process engineering; chemistry instrumentation and laboratory progression; materials synthesis and characterisation; chemical-process control; repeated chemical-design projects; or an equivalent chemical-engineering capstone. A 24-course UCR response would be a life-science or sustainability programme with isolated chemistry-related courses, not a defensible Chemical Engineering and Chemistry comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official structure accounts for all 180 EC as 120 EC of Chemical Engineering and Chemistry major and Bachelor College core formation, including the Bachelor Final Project, a 15-EC Impact of Technology learning line and 45 EC of electives. Current 2026-2027 TU/e course records confirm the integrated spine in calculus, practical and inorganic chemistry, chemical bonding and spectroscopy, organic chemistry, biochemistry and technology, thermodynamics, kinetics and electrochemistry, transport and separation, chemical reactors, materials characterisation, process technology and design, data and computational methods, challenge-based projects and the final project. These subjects are developed as a connected experimental and engineering sequence rather than as optional applications of biology, sustainability or mathematics.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry and HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory provide molecular, biochemical and one introductory laboratory strand. ENSGATE101 Sustainability Essentials I, ENSGATE201 Sustainability Essentials II, ENSSUST112 Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy, ENSDELT311 R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design provide environmental assessment, circularity, limited inorganic-chemistry context and systems design. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH312 Linear Systems, DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics, DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming and DISDATA111 Introduction to Data Science provide useful quantitative and computational foundations. The workbook nevertheless contains no staged general, inorganic, organic, analytical or physical chemistry curriculum; no chemical thermodynamics, reaction engineering, transport phenomena, fluid flow, heat and mass transfer, separation processes, unit operations, process dynamics and control, chemical-plant design or industrial scale-up; no sustained chemistry laboratory, spectroscopy, analytical instrumentation, materials synthesis and characterisation sequence; and no chemical-engineering design-project and final-project spine. HCBLIFE213 and HCBLIFE214 support biochemistry and introductory life-science laboratory work, while ENSDELT311 gives limited environmental and inorganic-chemistry context, but these isolated courses cannot support a coherent 24-course chemical-engineering programme.
